subject: community-medicine
title: Leprosy Elimination: Contact Chemoprophylaxis and Sparsh Drives

steps.title: Contact chemoprophylaxis with single-dose rifampicin
steps.tx: To break ongoing community transmission chains, national guidelines prescribe **single-dose rifampicin chemoprophylaxis** for all eligible household, neighbour and social contacts of newly confirmed leprosy cases. Administered as a weight-banded oral dose, typically six hundred milligrams for adults, this preventive intervention destroys subclinical bacillary loads in exposed contacts, reducing the risk of developing clinical disease by fifty to sixty percent over two years.
steps.say: Giving a single preventive dose of rifampicin to household and next-door contacts of newly diagnosed patients halves their chance of developing leprosy over the next two years.

nodes.label: Screening of household and neighbor contacts

steps.title: Contact screening and SDR eligibility rules
steps.tx: Before dispensing preventive medicine, health workers conduct rigorous **contact screening evaluation** to ensure that candidates do not already harbor active leprosy or active tuberculosis, have no known liver disease, and have not taken rifampicin in the preceding two years. Household contacts, family relatives and close residential neighbours residing within five houses undergo whole-body skin and peripheral nerve examination under adequate natural light before prophylaxis.
steps.say: Frontline workers examine every household member and immediate neighbours under bright daylight to verify they do not already have active leprosy before giving the preventive rifampicin pill.

steps.title: Annual new case detection rate as the core metric
steps.tx: While national elimination at the country level was declared in 2005 when prevalence dropped below one case per ten thousand population, epidemiologists prioritize the **annual new case detection rate** to evaluate true transmission. Calculated as total newly detected cases during the calendar year divided by the total population times one hundred thousand, this rate reflects active ongoing transmission and exposes undetected disease reservoirs across endemic districts.
steps.say: Prevalence alone can hide active transmission. The annual new case detection rate per hundred thousand population shows whether fresh infections are actually declining or still spreading.

steps.title: Child proportion and Grade 2 disability rates
steps.tx: Programme evaluators track two vital quality indicators: the **child proportion indicator**, which measures the percentage of new cases occurring in children under fifteen years, and the Grade 2 disability rate among new cases. A child proportion exceeding ten percent proves active recent community transmission, while a Grade 2 disability rate above five percent reveals substantial delays in diagnosis and treatment-seeking within the community.
steps.say: If more than ten percent of new patients are young children, infection is actively spreading today. A high rate of permanent deformity among new cases proves patients are arriving too late.

steps.title: Sparsh Leprosy Awareness Campaign
steps.tx: To combat social stigma and encourage voluntary presentation, the health ministry conducts the nationwide **Sparsh Leprosy Awareness Campaign** launched annually on World Leprosy Day on January thirtieth. The campaign mobilizes Gram Sabhas, village panchayats, schools and civil society organizations, reading an official anti-stigma charter, organizing street plays, and promoting the message that leprosy is completely curable and causes no permanent disability when diagnosed early.
steps.say: The Sparsh campaign launches every year on January thirtieth. Village councils and schools hold community rallies to shatter social stigma and urge people with skin patches to visit clinics.

steps.tx: Banners and pledge sheets mark a community rally against the stigma of leprosy. The **Sparsh Leprosy Awareness Campaign** opens nationally each year on World Leprosy Day, which falls on 30 January. Gram sabhas, village panchayats, schools, and civil society groups read an official anti stigma charter and stage street plays. The message is that leprosy is fully curable and need not leave permanent disability when the diagnosis is made early.
steps.say: Every 30 January the Sparsh campaign asks village councils, schools, and local groups to hold rallies and read an anti stigma charter. Street plays carry the point that leprosy can be cured and that early care prevents lasting disability.

steps.title: Active case detection campaigns in endemic blocks
steps.tx: In high-endemic districts, health authorities execute door-to-door **active case search campaigns**, pairing a female Accredited Social Health Activist with a male volunteer to examine every household resident. Operating with detailed microplans covering every village hamlet, teams examine male and female family members in separate private rooms with informed consent, uncovering hidden paucibacillary patches and early nerve enlargement before irreversible physical deformities can take hold.
steps.say: Two-person health teams visit every house in high-risk villages. Examining families in private rooms uncovers hidden patches early, protecting patients from permanent nerve injury.

steps.title: Slit skin smear technique and bacteriological index
steps.tx: Laboratory technicians confirm multibacillary infection using a **slit skin smear**, obtaining dermal tissue fluid from at least four anatomical sites, typically both earlobes and two active skin lesions. Using a scalpel blade to make a small incision while squeezing skin between fingers to produce an avascular field, the technician scrapes tissue fluid, heat-fixes the smear, and performs modified Ziehl-Neelsen staining using five percent sulfuric acid decolouriser.
steps.say: A slit skin smear pinches the skin to stop bleeding, makes a tiny nick, and scrapes tissue fluid from earlobes and lesions. Staining with acid confirms whether bacilli are present.

steps.tx: The blade nick on a pinched earlobe is how tissue fluid is taken for leprosy bacteriology. A **slit skin smear** samples at least four sites, usually both earlobes and two active lesions. Skin is squeezed to keep the field bloodless, a small incision is made, and fluid is scraped onto a slide. The smear is heat fixed and stained by a modified Ziehl Neelsen method that uses 5 percent sulfuric acid as the decolouriser, so acid fast bacilli can be seen.
steps.say: Skin is squeezed until it blanches, a tiny nick is made, and fluid is scraped from both earlobes and from active lesions. After acid decolourising stain, the smear shows whether leprosy bacilli are present.

steps.title: Bacteriological and morphological index calculation
steps.tx: Microscopists grade bacillary load using Ridley scale to determine the **Bacteriological Index**, ranging from zero for no bacilli in one hundred oil immersion fields up to six plus for more than one thousand bacilli and globi per single field. The Morphological Index calculates the percentage of solidly stained, uniformly cylindrical, living bacilli versus fragmented or beaded non-viable organisms, serving as an accurate biological marker of therapeutic responsiveness.
steps.say: The Bacteriological Index grades the density of bacilli on a scale from zero to six. The Morphological Index measures the percentage of living, solidly stained bacteria to monitor cure.

steps.title: Nikshay-like digital tracking for leprosy
steps.tx: To ensure treatment adherence and track post-cure surveillance, the national directorate implemented the **digital leprosy portal**, registering every beneficiary on a cloud database linked to national identity numbers. The portal generates automated reminders for monthly blister pick-up, tracks treatment completion rates, logs Grade 2 disability status, and triggers timely household contact screening to guarantee that chemoprophylaxis is administered to all eligible contacts.
steps.say: A dedicated digital portal tracks every leprosy patient from initial diagnosis to treatment completion. It issues blister refill reminders and schedules contact screening rounds.
